title: Drive to Kochkor & ride to Kol-Ukok Lake
desc: We start early from Bishkek and drive to Kochkor Village, gateway to the high lake of Kol-Ukok. Lunch waits at a local guesthouse before you meet your horse and settle into the saddle.

The trail begins gently along the Ukok River, then steepens through rugged country past lone herder houses. By evening you reach a yurt camp on the shore of Kol-Ukok, a fine first taste of nomad life in the mountains.
meals: Lunch at guesthouse, dinner at yurt

title: Ride over Kyzyl-Jar Pass to Ak-Kiya
desc: After breakfast you climb to the Kyzyl-Jar Pass at 3600 m, the highest point of the ride, with wide alpine views in every direction. A picnic lunch at the top makes the most of it.
From the pass you drop into the Kara-Kujur Valley and ride on to the remote village of Ak-Kiya, reaching it by early evening. A quiet walk and a home-cooked dinner round off the day.
meals: Breakfast at yurt, picnic lunch, dinner at homestay

title: Ride toward Dolon Pass
desc: You ride out through Ak-Kiya, past traditional homes and everyday village life, then climb into rougher hill country with rolling ridges and distant peaks. A mid-morning picnic gives the horses a rest.

The trail follows the ridges, crosses the Bishkek-Torugart highway briefly, and brings you to a yurt near the Dolon Pass. A shepherd family hosts you for the night with a hearty dinner and good company.
meals: Breakfast at homestay, picnic lunch, dinner at yurt

title: Ride into Ken-Suu Valley
desc: The morning climbs toward the Dolon Pass with views over the Ken-Suu Valley and the Kara-Unkur gorge. You pause for a relaxed picnic in a sheltered spot.

The afternoon is easier going, riding through the Ken-Suu Valley past open pastures, grazing sheep, and scattered yurts. A Kyrgyz family welcomes you for the night, with dinner by firelight under the stars.

title: Ride over Terskey-Torpu Pass toward Song-Kol
desc: After saying goodbye to your hosts, you ride up to the Terskey-Torpu Pass, where Song-Kol suddenly appears, turquoise and ringed by mountains. A picnic at the top gives the horses time to rest.
From there you descend through open grassland toward the lake's edge, reaching the quiet Kumduu-Suu Valley by day's end. A yurt set up by local herders waits for you, just short of the lake itself.

title: Ride along Song-Kol to Uzbek-Ashuu
desc: Today you take in Song-Kol up close, riding the open northern shore on smooth ground that is made for a relaxed canter, with the lake on one side and big horizons on the other.
Around midday you stop at a lakeside yurt for a warm lunch and a rest. The ride then continues gently to the Uzbek-Ashuu pasture, where you settle into a yurt for your last night in nomad country.

title: Ride to Kyzart & drive to Bishkek
desc: The last morning begins with breakfast and farewells, then a ride up to the Uzbek-Ashuu Pass at 3300 m for a final look back at Song-Kol before the trail descends toward Kyzart Village.

You part with your horses after seven days in the saddle and enjoy a well-earned lunch at the guesthouse. From there it is a drive back to Bishkek, the quiet nomad world slowly giving way to the city.
meals: Breakfast at yurt, lunch at guesthouse
